objective: Invite specific feedback on a free L/N pronunciation drill through one authentic first-party story, without implying clinical accuracy, customer outcomes, or public app-store availability.

supported_capabilities: Hear an L/N contrast and record one word
Inspect explainable practice feedback rather than a bare score
Switch practice among English, Mandarin, and Cantonese
Use the public browser version without creating an account

release_state.policy: This campaign links only the live PWA. Do not call either store version public or available until the corresponding storefront is independently verified.

audio_repair.pwa: The iPhone browser path now records one microphone stream, retains the waveform after Stop, and requires recognized text before showing or saving a score.
audio_repair.apple: iOS and embedded watchOS build 2 include the repair and are available through TestFlight; the same build is waiting for formal App Review.
audio_repair.android: Android build 3 includes the no-empty-score repair plus release-only microphone permission and non-resolving Stop fixes. A signed release-emulator test showed the live waveform, a completed Stop flow, and no score for silence.
audio_repair.claim_boundary: Describe scores as explainable coaching feedback, never as clinical assessment or guaranteed pronunciation accuracy.

android_test_build.policy: Use only for an explicit tester invitation after rechecking the exact artifact and tester access; it is not evidence of public Google Play availability.

media.content: First-party L-and-N screens, icon, and bundled synthetic light/night prompts in an English and Traditional Chinese vertical demonstration.
media.claim_boundary: The clip is a product demonstration, not a customer result, accuracy benchmark, medical assessment, or public-store availability claim.

linkedin.content:
I have trouble pronouncing L and N, so I built the practice tool I wanted.

Hear a pair, see the mouth and airflow cue, record one word, and get feedback you can inspect. The same four-minute drill works in English, Mandarin, and Cantonese.

It’s free and open source, and runs in the browser without an account:
https://l-and-n.lazying.art/

If you try it, tell me whether the mouth view actually makes the difference clearer.
linkedin.policy: This is a scheduled first-party product demonstration, not yet a public post, engagement, lead, or sale. Recheck delivery after the scheduled time before recording publication or outcomes.

reddit.policy: Answer the learner's question completely before mentioning the maintained PWA; disclose affiliation and do not reuse the LinkedIn announcement as a community reply.

x.policy: Do not duplicate the LinkedIn draft merely to increase channel count. Use a separate concise educational angle after current queue and provider-state review.

hackernews.policy: Do not draft or publish agent-authored comments.

funnel.policy: A draft, post, view, app test, comment, star, or store review state is not revenue. Record money only after a separately evidenced received payment.
